source.author: ov
source.text: Tabuerant cerae: nudos quatit ille lacertos, remigioque carens non ullas percipit auras, oraque caerulea patrium clamantia nomen excipiuntur aqua: quae nomen traxit ab illo.
source.text_original: Tabuerant cerae: nudos quatit ille lacertos, / remigioque carens non ullas percipit auras, / oraque caerulea patrium clamantia nomen / excipiuntur aqua: quae nomen traxit ab illo.
source.text_english: The wax had melted away; he shakes his bare arms, and lacking oars he catches no breezes at all, and his blue mouth, crying his father’s name, is taken up by the water; from him the sea took its name.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hanc Panope Dotoque soror laetataque fluctu prosequitur nitidis pariter Galatea lacertis alta petens: Siculo revocat de litore Cyclops.
reuse.text_original: hanc Panope Dotoque soror laetataque fluctu / prosequitur nitidis pariter Galatea lacertis / alta petens: Siculo revocat de litore Cyclops.
reuse.text_english: To this one Panope, and her sister Doto, rejoicing in the wave, and Galatea too, with gleaming arms, follows, seeking the deep: the Cyclops recalls her from the Sicilian shore.
